name: Hydrogen for refinery and ammonia feedstock
principle: Refineries (hydrotreating, hydrocracking) and ammonia plants are the largest hydrogen users. Refining used more than 43 Mt of hydrogen in 2024, 45% made on site from unabated fossil fuels and 35% as by-product; low-emissions hydrogen in refining was only about 250 kt. Southeast Asian refining used 1.3 Mtpa in 2024.

performance.basis: second largest after industry; growth only about 0.5 Mt

source.note: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025 (collected in corpus/iea-reports): refining demand

performance.metric: hydrogen demand in Southeast Asian refining, 2024
performance.basis: region has about 5.5 Mbpd refining capacity in 30 refineries

source.note: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025 (collected in corpus/iea-reports): Southeast Asia refining

costs.metric: levelised cost of hydrogen, unabated natural gas reforming
costs.basis: 2024 regional cost range, reflecting natural gas prices of USD 1.7-25/MBtu; figure values in USD (2024)

source.note: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025, Chapter 3 text on Figure 3.8 (page 93)

costs.metric: levelised cost of hydrogen, unabated natural gas reforming, STEPS 2030 projection
costs.basis: Stated Policies Scenario 2030, in USD (2024); larger drop at the high end as gas prices decline, partly offset by rising CO2 prices

source.note: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025, Chapter 3 text after Figure 3.8 (page 94)

costs.metric: levelised cost of hydrogen, natural gas with CCUS, 2022 gas-price episode
costs.basis: in the 2022 gas-price crisis, LCOH from unabated natural gas was just above USD 1/kg (nearly USD 2/kg with CCUS) in gas-producing regions and up to close to USD 9/kg in importing regions; figure values in USD (2024)

source.note: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025, Chapter 3 text on Figure 3.8 (page 93)

costs.metric: levelised cost of hydrogen, renewable electrolytic, STEPS 2030 projection
costs.basis: Stated Policies Scenario 2030, in USD (2024): lower end close to under USD 2/kg in China; USD 3-4/kg in Australia, Chile, Brazil, the Middle East and the United States

source.note: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025, Chapter 3 text on Figures 3.8 and 3.9 (pages 94 and 97)
IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, latest assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'Haber-bosch process using electrolytic hydrogen' 8 (2025)

advantages: Existing demand base for low-emissions hydrogen
